content: <@!185916549066915852> Kairo finds you after Ogden sent a messenger to find him.
"What is it, Goanhawe? I've been very busy with preparations for the expedition." They said it couldn't wait.
Preparations? The ship got attacked last night--and rumor is it's going to happen again tonight. What do you know about the Golden Dawn?

"Only that they wish to keep us from reaching our home. Truth is I know nothing of these maniacs who attacked the submarine. If you have any information that could aid us in defense, I would be very grateful. It is good to have an ally from home that I can depend on like you friend."

"I'll compose a report for you of what I know in a bit--I'm sorry to leave this conversation early, but I have to attend to Ebuc, he's very injured and I've been seeing to him all day." Goanhawe leaves the conversation and walks briskly out into <#636016776349745164>
That is quite alright friend. Thank you for your aid. We set sail soon m, I must continue preparing. Good bye.

Helga’s Mandatory Recreation and Omingmak milk Spa.
Probably the happiest place aboard the boat, Helga’s Mandatory Recreation is mandatory for all personnel. A fit body makes for a sharp mind, to the Gnomish Gnerman way of thinking. The Spa also contains an electric eel sensory deprivation chamber that opens to reveal a smugglers hold that is private to the OoK.
And then he makes a small, uncomfortable bed out of loose things. He sleeps.

A Full Accounting of my Time in the Golden Dawn
    Secrets and fear are the tradestuff of the Golden Dawn, and for this reason I will not give any of the names of members of the Golden Dawn in this chronicle. There are few of us left, and I hope that they will choose to leave of their own accord, motivated by love of their fellow man, rather than by fear of discovery.
    My time in the Golden Dawn began with a simple message I received while tracking the origin of an amulet of theirs that I found on a werewolf that had marked the Tir Na Nog a week before our departure. They promised knowledge and power, and told me they had many Uru members. The day before the summoner attacked the Tir Na Nog, I was told the Golden Dawn would create a distraction that would allow me to place a box in the ship, a small lead box that the Golden Dawn had couriered to me and that I had been instructed not to open or examine. The summoner breached the magical defenses of the Tir Na Nog in his attack, allowing multiple boxes to be taken aboard without raising any magical alarms. This, to the best of my knowledge, was the true purpose behind that attack on the Tir Na Nog. No members of the Golden Dawn knew of the details of the attack before it occurred, we were only told that we would be provided a distraction. All of us, however, are guilty of going through with the mission in spite of the body count that 'distraction' entailed.
    The next day, we were inducted into the Golden Dawn, and entered the foreboding mansion on Tottenham court. We were told that the mansion itself would be used to attack the Tir Na Nog, and that we were to assist in the Tir Na Nog's defense. Some hours before the mansion's attack, we were instructed to burn down Generous Jack's shop. I arrived at the scene to find Jack's shop already burning and watched as Jack fled from his shop and into the Thames. I attempted to retrieve his body to no avail. Others attempted the same later that night, again to no avail.

The last three months on the ship were quiet. I figured they would remain so until we reached Arcania. It seemed the Golden Dawn shared the goal of reaching her shores. 
    That quiet ended on the day the infernal contract was discovered. We were instructed to get Castor to sign it, and so I took it upon myself to go to Copper and let him know that he had an infernal contract. I did so by seeking the aid of Sir Wynne to translate, and when I saw that they intended to get Castor to sign it, I attempted to distance both myself and the Golden Dawn from the act by attacking Sir Wynne's character in a heavy-handed fashion. I then observed Castor and Copper discussing the matter in vague terms, until Fyr pulled Castor away, presumably to make things considerably less vague and to convince Castor to sign the contract. Seeing my part in this finished, I instructed another Golden Dawn member to make sure the deal was consummated while I waited in the Golden Dawn's chambers. Eventually, all but Rah arrived--the Golden Dawn member I had instructed to see the deal consummated arrived fuming. The contract had not been signed. Rah was forcibly teleported into the chambers and we were informed that he had given the names of most of our order to Amara and Castor. A vote was held, and Rah is executed by Power Word Kill. One who voted for his death was so overwhelmed by the events that their memory was struck as a mercy.

We were instructed to silence Castor and Amara. One of our order requested scrolls of modify memory, that we might do it without violence. But we lacked members available to cast the scrolls. I returned Rah to his bed, and then I told Amara that Rah wishes to speak with her in room 2. Once she arrived, I cornered her and explained that she and Castor would be in great danger so long as they knew the names of the members of the Golden Dawn, that we could protect Castor from harm by removing his knowledge of the names, but that there remained a danger that the memories will returned with a simple casting of lesser restoration. The scheme only worked as long as there was somebody we could trust willing to monitor him and make sure that either the memories never return or that they are erased each time that they return. Amara would need to be that somebody we could trust. She reluctantly agreed, and we went into Castor's room. She cast modify memory, and I went through his things until I found his journal. I ripped out the last few pages.

To the best of my knowledge at this point, the names of the Golden Dawn are safe, and we must merely weather the investigation of Rah's death. His body bears no marks, and his death was the result of a spell that could not be cast by any of our number. It was also my belief that we would have control over the autopsy and could report natural causes.
    Sir Wynne, due to my earlier attacks on their character, strongly suspects me of evil-doing, and monitors me with Fyr. I think, largely due to this and my frequent attempts to enter the med bay, the passengers begin to believe that I am the prime suspect, and Castor intends to try me. Amara is again conscripted, this time as my defender, this time with direct threats to Castor and her sister Ophelia from the head of my order. We are instructed to make it appear as though Amara has been thrown out of the Golden Dawn, so while everyone explores Mantopolis, I set Amara's room on fire. I am confident that I will survive the trial, but the court of public opinion has already declared me guilty, so I attempt to exonerate myself with Zone of Truth. I ask Leaf to cast Zone of Truth on me before the trial, where I will read a prepared statement. I find someone who I believe will be willing to cooperate in a scheme in order to gain access to the Golden Dawn. They will disguise themselves as me and read my prepared statement for me.
     The attempted exoneration goes extremely poorly. Leaf elects to try to control the situation by casting command and forcing my double to confess. He confesses to "not being without sin." She then casts the Zone of Truth under the condition that "others be allowed to ask questions." My double agrees, reads his statement under Zone of Truth, and then walks out of the Zone of Truth without answering any questions. I take his place before he is captured, whereupon I am thrown in to the brig.

The statement that my double read went as follows 'Greetings my fellow passengers. I stand before you, in this Zone of Truth, helpfully prepared by Leaf to allay your fears and suspicions. I have not killed Rahvioli. I was not in any manner involved in his death. I do not know who killed Rahvioli. I am not without sin, and I have acted in secrecy, but I am innocent of these crimes. Further, I would like to state that I am not a member of the Golden Dawn. I have never been a member of the Golden Dawn, and, excepting the Order of Kairo, I am not a member of any secret societies. I do not know the identities of the member or members of the Golden Dawn. I am not the one who has harmed Amara, and I am not the one who burned down her room. I do not know who did these things. Thank you all for coming, and being my witnesses. My statement is done. I will not be taking questions.'
Nearly every sentence in that statement could not have been spoken by me.

As I am dragged to the brig, I accuse everyone of mob justice, of deliberately sabotaging an infallible way of establishing truth, of this and that. I am trying to establish reason to refuse going under Zone of Truth again, should it come up. Sir Wynne has claimed to see an aura of transmutation on my double and I accuse them of being controlled by fiends. It won't win the court of public opinion, but it allows me to act as though I am not caught. I cast enhance ability (charisma) on myself so that I can truthfully say that I cast transmutation magic on myself that day to give myself a more authorative speaking voice. Various people come to chat, trying to extract a confession. I maintain my innocence. My attitude begins to change when I am taken up to drink and sing sea shanties on the island, and many, including many who strongly suspected that I may have been involved in Rah's death, treat me with uncalled-for kindness.

The head of my order has assured me it will protect its own. Yet all he has done is threaten Amara to be my defender. Even if I survive, I will be at best a pariah, useless to the Order. It was my desire to act as ambassador to the Urukocra in the Arcania, and I cannot do this as a pariah. I was promised knowledge and power for joining the order, and I have less now than I ever have. Meanwhile, those who should be my hated enemies refuse to hate me. I cannot bear it any longer. I return to the brig. Fyr comes to me and comforts me, despite my repeated cruelty to his master. Archivist Daysong comes to me, and we have a chat under wards that protect us from scrying from the head of my order. I'm ready to confess all, but he already knows.

I spend the next few days making peace with the fact that I am now opposed to the head of my order, that he can kill me with but a thought, and that there is nothing that anyone, not even Archivist Daysong can do about that. All I know is that I am determined not to hurt anyone as I have hurt Amara. I have set my intentions, and no threat from the head of my order, to my life or to another's, can deter me from this path.
Amara goes on a suicide mission in the abyss the next day. She does not return.
I talk to Archivist Daysong one more time, and prepare this chronicle.
One of our number is dead. Another is a close confidant of the captain. Another is not yet a member, but may be one yet (I beg of you, do not accept). Another has had their memory of Rah's death erased and then returned. The last writes this chronicle.
